exhibits.title: The Shrinking Glass of the Vault
exhibits.text: A cousin to the Divination wing's Mirror of Occlusion, though it hangs in a colder, deeper room. This glass does not hide meaning, it COMPRESSES it. Step before it holding a full canvas, 512 x 512 x 3 = 786,432 painted values, and your reflection shrinks to a dense little emblem of 64 x 64 x 4 = 16,384 numbers, roughly 48 times smaller, that still carries everything the picture MEANS. This is the VAE (variational autoencoder), and it is trained SEPARATELY and FROZEN before any diffusion begins. Its ENCODER folds the painting into a latent z; its DECODER unfolds z back into pixels, and the two are tuned so the round trip loses almost nothing you would notice. The whole reason this vault exists: painting directly in pixels is ruinously dear. A 512 x 512 image is 262,144 positions per channel, every one of ~1000 sampling steps drags the U-Net across the full-resolution feature maps, and self-attention costs O(n^2) in the count of positions. Pixel-space diffusion demanded datacenter GPU clusters. So the wizards of Latent Diffusion (LDM, which became Stable Diffusion) made a bargain: never diffuse in the great hall of pixels, diffuse inside this shrunken emblem instead. The U-Net that does the denoising NEVER sees a pixel. It is born, lives, and labours entirely inside the Glass, moving latents toward latents. Only at the very end does the DECODER open the Glass and let the finished latent bloom back into a 512 x 512 painting. Because the emblem is 48x smaller, the memory and compute fall by ~48x, the attention matrices shrink, and a 512 x 512 generation fits in about 8 to 12 GB. That single bargain is why Stable Diffusion ran on a gaming GPU in a student's bedroom while DALL-E 2 stayed locked in a datacenter.

exhibits.title: The Bargain: Two Journeys Through the Glass
exhibits.text: Learn the vault by its two rituals. TRAINING: take a real image, pass it once through the VAE encoder to get the clean latent z_0, then run the ordinary diffusion schedule ON z_0, add noise over t steps, and teach the U-Net to predict it back. The image is visited only to be encoded; thereafter the U-Net trains purely on latents. GENERATION: start from pure noise shaped like a latent, 64 x 64 x 4, run the reverse diffusion for its ~1000 (or, with better samplers, far fewer) steps to arrive at a clean z_0, and ONLY THEN hand z_0 to the VAE decoder, which unfolds it into the final 512 x 512 x 3 picture. Note the neat division of labour: the frozen VAE is the master of fine PIXEL detail, grain, edges, texture, while the U-Net is freed to worry only about SEMANTIC structure, the arrangement of things that makes an image mean something. Text guidance changes nothing about this shape: cross-attention simply lets the image-side queries, which now come from latent positions, attend to the words.

exhibits.title: What Attention Actually Squares
exhibits.text: A trap the careful apprentice must avoid. Attention does NOT square every scalar in the latent, it squares the number of SPATIAL POSITIONS. Flatten the 64 x 64 x 4 latent by its spatial grid and you get (4096, 4): n = 4096 tokens, each a 4-dimensional vector. The 4 channels ride along as the VECTOR DIMENSION; they are never squared. So the attention score matrix is (4096, 4096) ~ 16.7M entries, not 4096 x 4 anything. Whenever someone multiplies channels into the n^2, gently correct them: channels are the width of the message, not the number of messengers.

exhibits.title: Why the Top Floor Has No Attention
exhibits.text: 16.7M is still a heavy matrix to carry ~1000 times, so real U-Nets simply DO NOT run attention at the top 64 x 64 level, they use convolution only there. Attention begins one floor down. Walk the levels: 64 x 64 gives n = 4096 and n^2 ~ 16.7M (conv only, no attention); 32 x 32 gives n = 1024 and n^2 ~ 1.05M (attention starts); 16 x 16 gives n = 256 and n^2 ~ 65.5K (attention); 8 x 8 gives n = 64 and n^2 ~ 4.1K (attention). The principle is near-universal: CONVOLUTION, whose cost grows only LINEARLY in pixels, handles the expensive high-resolution top; ATTENTION, whose cost grows QUADRATICALLY, is spent only in the cheap, shrunken lower rooms where the position count is small. Which exact levels receive attention is a knob the architect sets, the `attention_resolutions` config field. The numbers shift between models (SD 1.5 uses a 64x64 latent with attention at 32/16/8; SDXL uses a larger 128x128 latent and moves the placement), so when you debug a specific model, read ITS config rather than assuming.

exhibits.title: The Two Journeys and the Cheap Lower Floors
exhibits.caption: Left: training encodes an image once, then diffuses the latent. Right: generation denoises noise into a latent, then decodes to pixels. Below: the U-Net's levels, with attention (quadratic) confined to the small lower rooms and conv (linear) holding the 64x64 top.

exhibits.title: The Compression Bargain, Drawn to Scale
exhibits.caption: The bargain of the Shrinking Glass in three tellings. First, drawn to scale: the gold emblem is the WHOLE latent set inside the pixel canvas, 64x64x4 = 16,384 numbers against 512x512x3 = 786,432, some 48 times fewer, with the areas true so the eye feels the shrink. Second, what shrinking buys on a log scale: 48x fewer numbers to store, 64x fewer spatial positions n, and because self-attention costs O(n^2), roughly 4,000x cheaper attention. Third, the pipeline: the frozen VAE encoder folds an image once into a clean latent z0, the U-Net diffuses entirely inside the latent for its ~1000 steps and NEVER sees a pixel, and only at the very end does the decoder unfold the finished latent back into a 512x512x3 painting. The VAE masters fine pixel detail so the U-Net is freed to worry only about semantic structure, which is why Stable Diffusion fit on a gaming GPU (~8-12 GB) while pixel-space diffusion needed datacenters.
